# Verified PDFium supply

This fork starts from the published `pdfium_dart` 0.3.1 Dart API and generated bindings, retained under its MIT licence. A narrow, explicit safety guard now restricts `FPDF_InitLibraryWithConfig` to non-null configurations with version 1–5, the complete ABI prefix represented by the retained struct. Versions 6–7 append fields in PDFium 8100 and throw before native lookup. `FPDF_InitLibrary()` used by pdfrx is unchanged. The original archive and library wrapper provenance is in `docs/implementation/evidence/16-dependency-audit/provenance-packages.json`. No generated FFI signature was changed.

Vital changes the native supply hook, package manifest and that single checked method boundary: remove workspace resolution for the local path dependency, add the already admitted crypto 3.0.7 for SHA-256, and replace the unverified 7811 network download with pinned local 8100 release archives. The root path override exists solely for this reviewed supply and security-currency patch. There is no target fallback. Android arm/arm64/x64 and Linux x64 are admitted; other targets fail closed until reviewed.

The GitHub release `chromium/8100` is immutable, published 12 October 2026. Each archive's independently recomputed digest matched the GitHub asset SHA-256 digest. `native/manifest.json` records source, archive hash and extracted library hash. The build hook validates both, validates any existing cached library instead of trusting its name, and declares the archive and manifest as input dependencies. The hooks runner independently hashes the emitted code-asset output; the output is not its own input dependency. SHA-256 verification executes on each hook execution. An unchanged warm build skips the hook; a changed input or output hash triggers it again. Builds perform no PDFium network download. A corrupt cached library is an error, not silently accepted or replaced. Delete only the specifically identified corrupt build output after investigation before retrying.

The four `.tgz` files under `native/` are pinned source runtime deliverables for offline builds, not task cache. Each includes its upstream licence bundle. Distributable licence texts are also retained under `docs/implementation/licenses/pdfium-8100/`. `docs/implementation/evidence/16-pdfium-8100/` records exact native provenance and all 455 existing bound function names being exported by all four binaries, plus ELF alignment/dependencies. The Android/Linux union of 21 exact notice files (root licence plus 20 dependency texts) is checked by `tool/probes/files/verify_pdfium_notices.py`. Behaviour/build verification remains necessary beyond symbol compatibility.

Remove this local patch when upstream supplies a current, verified native asset hook satisfying the same hash/offline/licence requirements. Do not overwrite or broaden this fork during unrelated dependency updates.

## Binding boundary

The generated declarations retain the upstream version 1–5 struct layout; no new FFI declarations were handwritten. The safety guard is the only generated-file patch. The obsolete ffigen block referencing absent 7811 headers was removed. This fork does not claim a complete 8100-generated API. Future regeneration requires an exact admitted generator, the retained 8100 headers and a reviewed API diff; it must preserve the guard until a complete layout is generated. The pinned archive header and SHA-256 are retained with the evidence. The native C compiler reports the 8100 host layout as 56 bytes with added fields at offsets 48/52; the Dart prefix is 48 bytes and its seven existing offsets are tested. Negative tests prove null/unsupported versions never reach symbol lookup. Those tests must accompany any regeneration or supported-version change.

`tool/probes/files/inspect_pdfium_abi.py` reproduces native exports, header identity, raw ELF output and C layout. `verify_pdfium_runner.py` requires the serialized project CLI lease; it temporarily corrupts only the specifically identified PDFium output, restores the original bytes in `finally`, and retains warm-skip/rerun evidence. It must never run alongside another build. No global cache or SDK configuration is changed.
